articles.title: How to Use Meta Muse as Your Personal AI Assistant
articles.content:
Good Morning,
This week we continue our hands-on AI guide series, by some of the most talented folk writing AI guides on Substack.
I really respect Product people in how they are adopting AI and the quality of their insights and their detailed early adoption notes. I asked to give AI Supremacy readers an easy to understand guide to Meta’s Muse.
Meta's Muse product was launched on September 8th, 2026 and is one of the most ambitious personal assistants in the world. Meta Muse is 56 days old and Muse Wonder Full is a decent model. Muse hit 10 Million downloads in its first forty days just in the U.S. and Canada.
Ship and scale products 10x faster with AI-powered playbooks, tools and community.
I also want to share some related minimalistic AI news related to our deep dive into Muse today.
A potential competitor of Meta’s Muse is Instinct. Instinct is developing a personal agent that can perform day-to-day tasks autonomously. In late September, did a surprise Series C for $1 Billion quadrupling its valuation to $10 billion driven by this trend of Personal Assistants. Learn about Instinct. It’s still in private access as its invite-only Beta continues.
Grok Bot limits: In a shocking development on November 1st, Elon Must tweeted about Grok Bot here1. What followed were sudden and arbitrary limits and throttling of SpaceXSI’s services, including Grok Bot. The Halloween surprise included weekly usage limits being unexpectedly maxed out, even if they hadn’t been using SpaceX’s agentic AI overnight. Grok Bot has been positioned as a success story and while it’s built by the incredible Cursor team, it’s not clear if SpaceX has the compute capacity. SpaceX had leased considerable compute capacity to Anthropic this year that boosted SpaceX Earnings in Neo Cloud revenue.
New Claude Limits: Anthropic will likely IPO in two weeks, recently has updated Claude Code to block requests aimed at recreating or cloning existing video games and blocking reverse-engineering tasks. Game devs report that the safeguard is overly aggressive. AI generated indie games are flooding platforms like Steam.
M&A Accelerates: AI-connectivity deal of the cycle. Marvell Technology’s $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum Holdings represents one of the largest mega-deals of the AI hardware boom. It’s a global market leader in photonics, optical communications, and industrial laser technologies. It’s a huge deal where Marvell’s will be able to push into optical connectivity for artificial intelligence data centers. Marvell benefits by monetizing the electronic and architectural side of the bandwidth bottleneck that enables them to better compete with Broadcom. Marvel’s stock is up 92% this year, where increasingly it appears like Broadcom and Marvell operate in a functional duopoly.
The AI IPO of the decade is nearly upon us.
Meanwhile Anthropic updated its S-1 filing, you can read the updated version here.
The company said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year.
It reported a $104 billion net loss during the period, where it had a loss of $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025.
Third-quarter revenue increased around 47%, a steep drop from 144% growth in Q2 and 132% in Q1, reaching $17 Billion in revenue with a net loss of $23.29 billion during its third quarter.
In the amended S-1, Anthropic said it has entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements with an aggregate committed spend of about $895.4 billion.
Sid is a Product Leader at Enterprise companies. He writes The Product Channel, a newsletter that helps people get their day-to-day done faster with AI, at work and at home. He publishes AI tool 101s, each one tested on his own work, with the prompts to copy.
“An AI tinkerer. I'm obsessed with helping you get good at using AI” -Siddhartha Saladi
To get all-access to Sid’s publication it costs around $15 a month or $99 a year. If guides like this might be useful to you.
Muse is if anything the first major personal assistant designed to execute real-world tasks autonomously rather than simply responding in a turn-by-turn chat format with a very big budget. Anthropic is testing Duet that I recommend for Small businesses, entrepreneurs, freelancers and business people. Muse’s early momentum is exciting but also daunting. Many retailers, marketplaces, banks and even Amazon have pushed back and blocked it.
However, I should reiterate that Meta also launched Muse for Small Businesses. More specialized version of Muse remain fairly promising. Knowing how to use these personal assistants, getting the most out of them and any tips and ticks are generally worthwhile.
After writing about the era of personal super-intelligent agents about a month ago, I wanted to know what living with one is actually like. Sid Saladi spent a month finding out. He gave Meta's Muse real jobs, from his food log to a refund Google first refused, and wrote up what worked and where it broke.
The author picks 5 low-hanging fruit tasks and and analyzes the performance. While doing a detailed walk-through guide, recommended rule settings and more.
By , October 2026
Read more

articles.title: Google has Succeeded in Disrupting Itself
articles.content:
Good Morning,
There are small signs beginning to appear that BigTech won’t be the same after the AI boom.
Just a little note on Alphabet’s bifurcating Earnings. Google just released maybe the most disappointing Earnings in its history. I don’t say that lightly. While its Search business declines, it’s investing into TPUs and Google Cloud successfully, finally diversifying its business model to be a bit more sustainable as a Hyperscaler incumbent.
The transition is so bumpy, you’d be hard pressed not to question the plan.
Google release Gemini 4 Carbon, their strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
Alphabet reported negative free cash flow (FCF) of $9.07 billion during the third quarter.
Google’s Capex rose 114% y/y to $51.4bn (below est $55.8bn). But operating cash flow fell 13% y/y to $42.3bn, far short of the $53.9bn consensus.
Capex is eating into Operating cash flow.
Google Cloud revenue doubled year-over-year, reaching $30.7 billion (up 103% YoY from Q3 2025).
Cloud operating income tripled to $11.1 billion, expanding the unit's operating margin to 36.2%.
Alphabet reported free cash flow of (negative) -$9.07 billion in Q3 2026.
Long-term debt is up +479% in a year, to $125.1B. Not counting debt off the books obviously.
Incumbents won’t survive the way we remembered them, the shift is already occurring.
There are serious concerns for Hyperscalers and their Capex to negative FCF. Capital expenditure ballooned to $51.4 billion in Q3 (+114% YoY), primarily allocated to data center expansions, server hardware, and TPU inventory buildouts. Google’s AI chips (TPUs) are going to be a great business, likely the number #2 ahead of AMD chasing Nvidia by the end of the decade.
Google’s Cash burn is not great: Massive CapEx outlays, paired with a $5.2B European Commission regulatory fine payment, resulted in a negative free cash flow of -$9.1 billion for the quarter.
Google’s FCF was essentially $7 Billion less than analysts expected. The stock will have a likely hard end to the week. . (Down 9% after hours on Oct 28).
Google Search and YouTube growth is anemic, certainly not what we’ve expected from BigTech over the last few decades. They are essentially being beaten in AI by both Anthropic and OpenAI. Where are the bright spots?
But for how many days, weeks and can they replicate it in a good cadence?
Google’s revenue is still $127.6 Billion and grew 25%, but there are structural issues now at the company. Spending big for an uncertain future: Alphabet maintained its full-year capex forecast after lifting guidance to between $195 billion and $205 billion during Q2.
TPU sales are included in Google’s Cloud Revenue, so they can pretend to be something they are not.
Post Q3 Earnings, the future of Google is now open for debate.
So many dualities in Alphabet’s Earnings. So while outbound search clicks from Google to external websites are in a state of measurable (and incredible) decline, this even as total Google search query volume remains high or continues to grow. How do you monetize zero click journeys well? It’s the beginning of the end of an era.

Leave a comment

So while outbound search clicks from Google to external websites are in a state of measurable (and incredible) decline, this even as total Google search query volume remains high or continues to grow. With the release in of Claude Duet in research preview, sign up to the waitlist, and the dominance of Opus 5.5 since it came out in late September, I am fairly optimistic about the prospects of Anthropic. Full disclosure as things stand right now, I’m more bullish on Anthropic than I am on OpenAI. Going IPO first matters and getting that $100 Billion kickstart for compute is the right timing before the slowdown.
I went through the S-1 and curated some of the best infographics to quickly understand it.

If Anthropic is able to diversify well into finance, science and research, law, pharma, biotechnology and physical AI models and software, it’s a pretty exciting thing to witness. The entire Generative AI hype cycle depends on their execution in 2027 and 2028.
The S-1 is going to fill in the blanks and give us more clarity in the coming weeks. Here’s what we know.

Let that sink in:
With the latest batch of updates, I’m more confident in Anthropic’s approach to finance.
I believe the Anthropic IPO goes live on November 19th, just around three weeks from now.
While the current preliminary first version of the S-1 skipped Q3, we have data from OpenRouter that shows Anthropic’s incredible momentum in October:

But its Enterprise tools and research products are getting more precise with better integrations. While this is not an endorsement to buy the IPO, I do think exploring these AI tools for equity and stock research makes a lot of sense, no matter your level of market participation or interest in being an early AI adopter.

You can find more of his recent interviews with Substack investing, FinTwit and equity folk here. He moved to Ghost for a time but is now back on Substack.
If you want to dig deeper to get full access to the work of someone that’s been studying Asian equities for nearly two decades, consider a full sub to Asian Century Stocks. In particular for me, Michael’s Thematic reports are legendary.
One way to think of using Claude for Equity Research is the following:
Research
Projects
Skills

Before we begin, here are some of the easiest low-hanging fruit to use Claude for due diligence in equity research for non-financial beginners and the new generation of finance writers (I cover emerging technologies, especially Space-tech):
Earnings Call & Transcript Analysis: Drop a 50-page 10-K, 10-Q, or an earnings call transcript into Claude.
Competitor Benchmarking (Comps): Upload financial statements or reports for two or three competing companies in the same sector. Ask Claude to structure their revenue growth, gross margins, R&D spend, and cash conversion cycles into a clean comparative table.
Drafting Investment Memos: Use Claude to synthesize your thesis. Provide your raw notes, target financials, and risks, and ask Claude to structure them into an institutional-grade investment memo or due diligence report matching your preferred formatting style.
Use Claude Projects: Create a dedicated project space for each stock or sector you are researching. Upload baseline documents (historical annual reports, investor day presentations, and your own running thesis notes) into the project knowledge base so Claude retains context across multiple prompts.
Thesis Arguments: Ask it to build a bull case and a bear case for a stock or fund. Seeing the strongest arguments on both sides is a good guard against confirmation bias.
Starting a deep dive a) Business model breakdown: Ask how the company makes money, its revenue segments, customers, pricing power, and unit economics. b) Industry context: Have Claude map the competitive landscape, market structure, key trends, regulatory exposure, and what drives profitability in the sector. c) Moat analysis: Ask it to assess competitive advantages (network effects, switching costs, scale, brand, IP) and what could erode them. d) Key questions list: Ask for the 10 to 15 questions an analyst should answer before forming a view on this company.
Reading Primary Documents: e.g. Quarter-over-quarter changes: Ask what changed in risk factors, guidance, or accounting policy between two filings.

Live portfolio analysis: with Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), users are plugging Claude directly into live financial databases and brokerages.

articles.title: SpaceX merge with Tesla is on the Horizon
articles.content:
This Newsletter is called AI Supremacy and so part of my mission to consider various possibilities in the future of AI. But what if the future of Space-technology1 and AI are linked? And of recent increasing relevance, are the politics of Elon Musk even compatible with the stories of the future he is known for? Is the aging Tycoon still investible? 2 I’m looking for diverse opinions on this:
Lately I’ve been thinking about the merger of SpaceX and Tesla, which seems like it’s 95% going to happen soon. There are apparently “committees” at both Tesla and SpaceX looking into the merger. In recent years I’ve become a lot more interested in space-technology and in recent months more interested in National Defense with the Iran and Ukraine conflicts both seemingly escalating. When it came out that Elon Musk ordered Starlink to be throttled (speed restriction) for Ukraine, it got me a bit concerned.
Musk said on SpaceX's earnings call that the two companies have formed committees of independent directors to explore the possibility of a deal.
On the SpaceX Earnings call he basically said Tuesday that he would like to see the consolidation of his business empire by formally merging his two largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla. We know that consolidation is quickly approaching, either in 2027 or 2028 itself.
Elon Musk already has unprecedented control over SpaceX shares and owns about one fifth of Tesla. A combined entity is an incredible concentration risk, where Tesla continues to build inside of China. If SpaceX and Tesla combined it would be in the area of a corporation with a market cap of around $3.5 Trillion dollars. To put things in perspective that’s about equal to the GDP of France.
Elon Musk has a few big projects that could benefit from having a more diversified company with Tesla:
Scale Starlink
Dramatically increase launch cadence of Starship
Scaling own AI chips: Terafab
Winning the race to Orbital Compute (Datacenters in space)
Scaling Energy to compete with China
Winning the robotics and Physical AI race
Contributing to founding a sustainable Lunar Base (and colony)
Colonizing Mars, and contributing to making civilization multi-planetary to increase our chances for survival
With a bigger company, and one that he has more full control over, Elon Musk would be able to do a huge amount of M&A to ramp up SpaceX into a fairly large monopoly on the frontier of the Space economy, robotics, AI and AI compute infrastructure.
Tesla: Musk holds approximately 15% to 20% of equity (around 20% including vested options).
SpaceX: Musk holds approximately 40% to 42% of economic equity, but maintains over 80% voting power due to SpaceX’s super-voting Class B share structure.
So if you do the math, Musk would alone control in the area around 35% to 42% of total economic equity in the combined company with far higher voting rights.
Elon Musk could do significant M&A in semiconductors, aerospace, space-connectivity, and even National Defense, acquiring someone like Andruil, advanced manufacturing companies (e.g., Hadrian) and Physical AI software brain companies for humanoids. The stock share leverage of a combined entity of SpaceX and Tesla would give the company a lot of optionality and Musk would be able to dominate the future of Space.
How do you call a company a monopoly when it’s at the frontier of many rather high-risk and speculative emerging technology projects? SpaceX could also be scaled into National Defense entity that becomes weaponized for a kind of peculiar world domination for an oligarch class. Starlink has been incredible implicated in politics and geopolitics. Whatever the legacy of Elon Musk, this entity is likely going to be his last chance.
Tesla brings manufacturing scale, Energy, batteries, EVs, and robotics to the table. SpaceX brings launch dominance in rockets, a struggling xAI business that got stronger with Cursor3, Starlink global connectivity4, aerospace engineering with more shared projects like AI chips via Terafab. Is the combined entity better positioned to achieve what Elon Musk hopes to achieve? It would appear so. The combined entity would be better positioned for the large capex required and aggressive M&A that would be needed.
Tesla in 2026 will spend around $20 Billion in Capex, while SpaceX will likely do around $65 Billion. That’s $85 Billion of Capex just in 2026. Tesla has around $16 Billion of debt, SpaceX have closer to $40 Billion of debt. There’s no guarantee this would work out. SpaceX becoming profitable by being a Neo Cloud is not a great sign for its long-term financial sustainability.
A merger of Tesla with SpaceX was always part of the plan obviously for Elon Musk:
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions,” he said, but he added that “I think it would be a good idea.”
Elon Musk sees himself as a visionary and a combined entity gives him a longer career to explore that vision. If the AI bubble pops there will be a lot of interesting AI startups, Physical AI, Inference AI chip and semiconductor companies on sale, that SpaceX could acquire.
In harsher times, SpaceX could cherry pick bleeding AI, aerospace and space-technology startups while attracting more talent to its side with more financial leverage.
Elon Musk is part of a group of Silicon Valley tycoons who believe the era of energy abundance, superintelligence and multi-planet human capability is right around the corner. They believe having more agents and robots than people is a good idea, that will lead to a better life where off-world infrastructure enobles us on Earth5.
SpaceX, Tesla and all of Musk’s companies already share talent, have circular vendor financing and investments, share major infrastructure projects, that can be bundled into Musk’s evolving grand vision for the future of humanity.
For instance one of the new promises is that SpaceX is positioning orbital data centers (powered by abundant solar energy in space) as a major future revenue source and one of the keys to dominate the future of AI and compute. Given how poorly Tesla handled its robotaxi promises it will be interesting to see if the combined entity can fulfil any, some, or all of these grand projects, dreams and promises.
Now that SpaceX went public with the largest initial public offering on record - the combined entity would have a fairly diversified business model that could super-charge even grander ambitions. Albeit perhaps, with a limited real-world actual impact on consumers and civilization.
Bundling and merging Tesla into SpaceX also enables the company to hide some of its less than stellar aspects into yet another hype cycle. Tesla’s Q3 Earnings were not good where operating income plunged 56% year-over-year to $718 million as operating expenses jumped 39%. Deliveries and automotive revenue were both down.
SpaceX will require stupendous R&D, gigantic Capex6 and nearly flawless execution to pan out in accordance with the words of Elon Musk. That’s highly improbable. But doing massive and aggressive M&A might be the only way to keep the story alive, and a combined entity can do that much more efficiently than keeping the companies separate.
SpaceX began trading on the NASDAQ exchange in New York City at $135 a share, valuing SpaceX at nearly $1.8 trillion. The stock is now trading around $146. Tesla still somehow has a market cap of $1.5 trillion and while it’s not great for shareholders to combine the entities, it will happen. Elon Musk is the most consequential paper Trillionaire on the planet.
Production of Optimus humanoid robots has started on high-volume lines in Fremont and SpaceX’s AI business is hopefully just getting started. Starship being fully reusable and ramping up cadence opens up more possibilities for Space, aerospace and National Defense supremacy.
The merger will face scrutiny by US regulators but doing it (rushing it) while Trump is still POTUS is the goal. SpaceX also in recent months said they will build a massive new $100 billion spaceport named Starbase, in Louisiana in Vermilion Parish along the Louisiana Gulf Coast.
Tesla has a Forward P/E of 182, and SpaceX has an equally aspirational market valuation. Musk’s only hope is to do a massive Space-tech roll-up and spend big on compute and hope it pans out. But if you are investing in the combined entity, you are essentially investing in Elon Musk and the power of American capital, against all odds, including China. Musk’s politics is also a significant business risk, as recently he has committed roughly $366 million to the 2026 midterm election, with much of it aimed at preserving or expanding Republican power in Washington. But at 55, some of Musk’s magic and perhaps his sanity has declined. A projection of an almost childlike masculinity7 and transcendental con.
Those are big rockets you have sir. I hear you want to build a lot of robots. But the majority of Elon Musk’s vision remains highly speculative, with timelines that rarely match up with reality. Tesla makes 85% of its revenue from selling electric vehicles. It’s a car manufacturer pretending to be something more even after all these years. SpaceX makes the vast majority of its revenue from Starlink and selling compute as a Neo Cloud. It could take the combined entity easily a decade to take a meaningful step closer to its vision. As Tesla Robotaxis have demonstrated, that vision can also come a decade late, or not at all.
Some call Musk a genius, a visionary, a technological fraud or a corrupt tycoon, but the future is self-interested. SpaceX will still have to fight for its survival. The combined Tesla and SpaceX entity could have some serious geopolitical, China8 and Succession issues and challenges ahead9.
Orbital compute in Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO), could fundamentally alter and radically change the relationships between the future of AI and Space-technology companies.
Elon Musk is a figure whose legacy is deeply complex, polarising, and far from invisible. A hero to some, a villain to others and a path that China has and will likely supplant.
Only after a $60 Billion Acquisition. Not earned.
Starlink that has long been considered the key revenue growth driver of the company pre 2027.
Many are starting to question the human benefits and social value of Elon Musk’s companies and future vision.
The Space Neo Cloud, the original SNC, a weird convergence of low-earth-orbit infrastructure and dirty datacenters.
With significant characteristics of Asperger's syndrome and interpersonal narcissism with seemingly limited capabilities for empathy.
Tesla relies heavily on China for manufacturing (Giga Shanghai) and market demand. Conversely, SpaceX is a key U.S. defense contractor deeply integrated with national security, launch systems, and military communications. These conflicts of interest make Elon Musk unreliable.
Where Elon Musk owning too many SpaceX shares means that its biggest problem will be Elon Musk, and also what happens to the company after he is gone.
President Donald Trump awarded Elon Musk the National Medal of Science on October 8, 2026, during the “Science: A New Golden Age Summit”. The National Medal of Science is the highest honor the United States bestows in science and engineering. Elon Musk has been a major donor where during the 2024 presidential election cycle, Elon Musk spent roughly $250 million to $290 million specifically backing Donald Trump's campaign including using his ownership of Twitter/X for Trump’s campaigns. On X, Musk posted or reposted hundreds of messages in support of Trump to his 200+ million followers, generating tens of billions of views.
Ahead of Germany's federal elections, Musk openly endorsed the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), declaring that "only the AfD can save Germany".
European officials explicitly labeled Musk's posts and platform changes as a form of foreign political interference. His abuses of power include interference in the political processes of Brazil, France, United Kingdom and other countries.
Elon Musk’s Starlink Ukraine and Department of Government Efficiency (DODGE) interference are significant dents in his global reputation and beyond the scope of this article. His increasing geopolitical controversies, challenges facing his core business ventures and polarizing conduct add to the already considerable concentration risk of whatever SpaceX becomes.
Whether you are a fan or a critic of Musk, he’s putting oligarchs front and center with regards to the power that will come with technological progress in the 21st human century of history. SpaceX is as much an experiment in Moon shots as it is a diversifying company with perceived value mostly based on Elon Musk’s own reputation.
